progress: Mixed, a strategy text located and held while the document carries no date of its own and disagrees with itself about its horizon
summary: The [National AI Strategy text](2024-11-21-zambia-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy) was located in the copy lodged with an international policy observatory, and the ministry says the [strategy is nearing the end of its cycle](2026-08-17-zambia-ai-sovereignty-conditions-china-cooperation) and due for review.
developments:
The document carries no date of its own — no adoption date and no month in 121,000 characters of extracted text — and is dated here from the ministry's own launch announcement ([text](2024-11-21-zambia-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy)). It disagrees with itself about its horizon: the cover reads 2024-2026 and every running header reads 2025-2027. No first-party copy was located ([text](2024-11-21-zambia-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy)).

The permanent secretary said in August 2026 that the strategy is nearing the end of its cycle and due for review; a successor reading is an inference from the dates and is stated in no source held ([review](2026-08-17-zambia-ai-sovereignty-conditions-china-cooperation), [partnership](2026-08-07-zambia-china-explore-deeper-ai-partnership-to-accelerate-digital-transformation), [leadership](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge)).

A regional artificial-intelligence strategy sensitisation workshop was launched in the capital: the country is drafting a national instrument while helping shape the regional one that would frame it ([regional](2026-07-14 Zambia and COMESA Launch AI Initiative to Advance Regional Digital Transformation)).

progress: Mixed, two 2025 Acts in force with their investigatory powers court-gated while a threatened legal challenge has produced no record
summary: The [Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025](2025-04-15-zambia-cyber-security-act-no-3-of-2025) and the [Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025](2025-04-15-zambia-cyber-crimes-act-no-4-of-2025) are both in force, and the investigatory and interception powers in them are court-gated.
developments:
The gazetted text of the security Act was acquired from the National Assembly's own directory; it commenced on 12 May 2025 by statutory instrument ([Act](2025-04-15-zambia-cyber-security-act-no-3-of-2025), [signature](2025-04-15-zambia-cyber-security-act-no-3-of-2025)).

Enforcement of the crimes Act was declared fully operational in July 2026. The gazetted texts of both Acts are now held, and the investigatory powers in the crimes Act and the interception power in the security Act are both court-gated; the claim that the 2025 Acts authorise interception without prior judicial review is not borne out, while the presidential-control half of that claim is ([enforcement](2026-07-21-zambia-cyber-crimes-act-enforcement-begins), [warning](2025-04-18-us-warns-citizens-surveillance-law), [compliance](2026-07-22-zambia-cyber-crimes-act-compliance), [freedom](2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition)).

The Law Association was reported set to mount a challenge in April 2025; the single held source is a lede-only capture and the absence of any subsequent record is itself the finding ([challenge](2025-04-22-laz-legal-challenge-cyber-laws)).

summary: The [Data Protection Act 2021](2026-07-21-zambia-cyber-crimes-act-enforcement-begins) is named as part of the operative framework, and a reported Cabinet repeal intent has produced nothing in sixteen months.
developments:
The Act's number and year of enactment are not established beyond 2021, and the reported repeal intent has produced nothing on the record in sixteen months ([framework](2026-07-21-zambia-cyber-crimes-act-enforcement-begins), [safeguards](2024-09-17 DPI Safeguards come online in Zambias next phase of digital integration), [freedom](2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition)).

A statute whose own enactment reference cannot be established, under a repeal intent that has produced nothing, is the legal basis under which the identity register, the health record and the refugee database all operate.

summary: A [Postal and Courier Services Bill 2026](2026-07-23-zambia-postal-courier-services-bill-2026) went to public written submissions, replacing a 2009 Act that also underwrites postal banking and financial services.
developments:
Submissions closed on 27 July 2026 ([bill](2026-07-23-zambia-postal-courier-services-bill-2026), [submissions](2026-07-24-zambia-postal-courier-legislation-modernisation-public-submissions)).

The 2009 Act underwrites postal banking and financial services, so its replacement governs the postal service's agency-banking role — which makes a postal bill a payments instrument.

Submissions closed one working day after the consultations ended, and it is the only open public call for written comment on a domestic instrument the base holds for the whole window ([consultation](2026-07-24-zambia-postal-courier-legislation-modernisation-public-submissions)).

summary: The [mobile money levy](2026-03-01 Mobile Money Taxes and Affordability in Sub-Saharan Africa) rate doubled during 2025, dated only to the year, and the source is an industry body arguing against such levies.
developments:
The doubling is dated only to the year, so it cannot be placed inside or outside the window ([levy](2026-03-01 Mobile Money Taxes and Affordability in Sub-Saharan Africa)).

Naming the source's interest matters here: an industry body arguing against mobile money levies is the only account of this one, and no government or regulator statement of the rate or its yield is held.

summary: A [Cabinet directive on open-source technology](2026-06-17 Zambia's govt leans towards open-source) was issued to ministries, reported only in an excerpt of a trade-press article with no government publication held.
developments:
It was issued alongside the spatial data infrastructure launch in June 2026 ([directive](2026-06-17 Zambia's govt leans towards open-source)).

No government publication of it is held. Officials elsewhere in this ledger name fragmented, vendor-locked systems as a governance and legal problem rather than a technical one, which is the case the directive would answer — and the directive itself cannot be read.

summary: The [data protection commissioner](2026-07-31-civil-society-condemns-alleged-sms-linking-cash-transfers-to-voting-for-ruling-upnd) was asked by nine civil-society organisations to examine a beneficiary contact list, and nothing in the base shows the regulator acting.
developments:
The regulator exists and travels — it appeared at an international identity event — and nothing in the base shows it acting ([commissioner](2026-07-31-civil-society-condemns-alleged-sms-linking-cash-transfers-to-voting-for-ruling-upnd), [freedom](2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition), [engagement](2026-05-18-zambia-id4africa-multi-sectoral-engagement)).

Tenders were opened in August 2026 for a data protection compliance management system and for guidelines consultancy; these are tenders rather than awards, with no value, delivery date or statement of the commission's current caseload or enforcement record held ([tender](2026-08-10-zambia-dzap-data-protection-compliance-system), [guidelines](2026-08-10-zambia-dzap-data-protection-guidelines-consultancy)).

A regulator with no recorded action, procuring the system that would let it record action, is the position.

summary: A national was [elected Secretary-General of the continental telecommunications union](2026-07-27-atu-cpl26-abuja-declaration-sg-election-full-record) on the fourth round, and the country gains the secretariat and loses the council seat in the same cycle.
developments:
The election was won with 21 of 34 votes at a plenipotentiary conference, for a term beginning January 2027 ([election](2026-07-27-atu-cpl26-abuja-declaration-sg-election-full-record), [conference](2026-07-24-atu-cpl26-abuja-official)).

A declaration on meaningful connectivity was adopted at the same conference; it is a regional commitment with no domestic implementing measure in this base ([declaration](2026-07-27-atu-cpl26-abuja-declaration-sg-election-full-record), [connectivity](2026-07-25-atu-abuja-declaration-meaningful-connectivity-cpl26-thesun)).

Holding the continental secretariat while the national artificial-intelligence strategy is undated and the data-protection regulator has no recorded action is the shape of this unit's international position.

summary: A [regional programme steering committee](2026-07-30-comesa-idea-3rd-project-steering-committee) convened in the capital, the programme's stated policy and oversight body held by a regional body rather than by member states.
developments:
The third steering committee convened in July 2026, alongside the programme's annual digital forum ([committee](2026-07-30-comesa-idea-3rd-project-steering-committee), [forum](2026-07-27-comesa-idea-annual-digital-forum-launch-lusaka), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094))).

Policy and oversight for a national digital programme sitting with a regional secretariat rather than with member states is a governance arrangement the record states and nowhere explains.

summary: [Quarterly network-performance reporting](2026-05-15-zambia-approves-k255m-digital-infrastructure) was announced, and a provincial minister names four districts where poor service blocks access to social cash transfers and farm input subsidies.
developments:
Both regulator items behind the enforcement regime are paywalled ledes ([reporting](2026-05-15-zambia-approves-k255m-digital-infrastructure), [disruption](2025-06-13-zicta-investigating-internet-disruption), [action](2026-02-17-zicta-action-mobile-operators-poor-network)).

Naming districts where poor service blocks social cash transfers and farm input subsidies makes quality of service a benefits-delivery question rather than a consumer one.

Health ministry ICT standards issued in January 2014 are the oldest instrument in this ledger and the only national sectoral data standard the base holds for the country ([standards](2014-01-01-moh-zambia-ict-standards-and-guidelines)).

summary: [Observer missions issued preliminary statements](2026-08-15-zambia-eu-eom-preliminary-statement-digital-systems) on digital systems in the 2026 general election, and a [consent judgment](2026-08-05-keepiton-government-of-zambia-must-uphold-human-rights-and-ensure-unrestricted-internet-access) requires a reason for any internet interruption within 36 hours.
developments:
Four observer missions and a media body issued preliminary statements in August 2026; no final observer report, government response or electoral commission account of the accreditation and register decisions is held ([statements](2026-08-15-zambia-eu-eom-preliminary-statement-digital-systems), [media](2026-08-17-zambia-misa-regional-media-digital-rights-statement), [registration](2026-08-15-zambia-au-comesa-eom-preliminary-statement-digital-registration), [assessment](2026-08-14-zambia-ccmg-post-election-assessment-zambia-monitor)).

The consent judgment was entered after election-period blocking in August 2021 and requires a reason for any interruption within 36 hours; it is known to the base only through a coalition letter ([judgment](2026-08-05-keepiton-government-of-zambia-must-uphold-human-rights-and-ensure-unrestricted-internet-access)).

The Human Rights Commission considered 105 alleged violations and resolved 62; the listed remedies are administrative rather than adjudicative, and no sanction, compensation or determination is reported ([cases](2026-08-01-hrc-alarm-hate-speech-online-abuse-election)).

summary: A [K255 million digital infrastructure and quality-of-service allocation](2026-05-15-zambia-approves-k255m-digital-infrastructure) was announced as approved, with the stage unclear and no funding source named.
developments:
Approved is the source's word, and whether this is a cabinet approval, an appropriation or an in-year release is not stated; the amount is carried in local currency only and no funding source is named ([allocation](2026-05-15-zambia-approves-k255m-digital-infrastructure), [record](2026-01-01-zmb-2026-govt-digital-infra-qos)).

It is the only domestic financing figure in this ledger. Every other instrument here is externally financed or company-reported.

summary: A [digital acceleration project](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD) was board-approved in September 2025 as the fifth operation of a multiphase regional programme, with expected disbursement of US$6 million in the lender's 2026 financial year.
developments:
The programme envelope is US$2.48bn across fifteen countries ([project](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094)), [rollout](2026-01-05 Zambia programs national digital ID rollout for year-end)).

A rural connectivity project has a stated closing date of December 2025; its implementing agency is a road fund agency, which does not sit easily with the broadband description, and it should be treated as suspect before use as evidence of digital financing ([rural](2017-05-04-wb-zmb-001-zambia-improved-rural-connectivity-project)).

A regional science and technology accelerator is at expressions-of-interest stage: the fund is resourced, the delivery consortium is not chosen, and no national allocation is stated ([accelerator](2026-08-11-fcdo-sta-s-southern-africa-programme)).

summary: A [digital lender announced a K500m expansion](2026-07-27-lupiya-zambia-k500m-digital-lending-expansion) on its tenth anniversary, a forward intention by the lender itself with no external financier or named recipient.
developments:
The announcement was made in July 2026 ([lending](2026-07-27-lupiya-zambia-k500m-digital-lending-expansion)).

Development-finance equity in the independent tower portfolio exited in March 2021 and a US$75m loan was fully disbursed from that year ([towers](2015-01-01-bii-zmb-001-ihs-zambia-equity-investment-telecoms-tower)); the over-1,700 tower figure is the financiers' own and is not dated more precisely than 2021 ([towers](2015-01-01-bii-zmb-001-ihs-zambia-equity-investment-telecoms-tower), [loan](2021-01-01-ifc-zmb-001-ihs-zambia-ifc-loan-covid-relief)).

Two private-capital records, one an intention and one five years old, is the whole of non-state finance here.

summary: Four memoranda were signed — [digital identity with a neighbour](2025-10-03 Zambia plans domestic digital ID development with help from international partners), a [government compact with the payments association](2026-02-27 Zambia partners with PAYZ to boost financial inclusion), a [bilateral between two external organisations](2025-11-20-undp-tbi-mou-zambia), and a [card partnership](2026-06-03-zoyk-visa-digital-payments-partnership) — and none publishes a value.
developments:
The identity memorandum was reported signed with the signing date not established, and no value, duration or workplan is stated ([identity](2025-10-03 Zambia plans domestic digital ID development with help from international partners)).

The payments compact followed a State House meeting with no document, value or target published ([compact](2026-02-27 Zambia partners with PAYZ to boost financial inclusion)).

The third is a bilateral between two external organisations coordinating their support to government, with no value, duration or termination terms disclosed and the text unpublished ([coordination](2025-11-20-undp-tbi-mou-zambia), [rollout](2026-01-05 Zambia programs national digital ID rollout for year-end)); the card partnership reports no value, volume commitment or launch product ([card](2026-06-03-zoyk-visa-digital-payments-partnership)).

progress: Mixed, a backbone extension financed and 0 per cent drawn while the two national fibre-length figures cannot be reconciled
summary: The [backbone extension financing stood at 0 per cent disbursement](2017-01-01-eximbank-cn-zmb-005-china-eximbank-provides-3332-million-preferential) as of July 2022 — the largest single undrawn digital-infrastructure commitment the base holds — and the two [national fibre-length figures](2026-05-15-zambia-approves-k255m-digital-infrastructure) are irreconcilable.
developments:
Corruption allegations from a former utility board chairman are on the record against the undrawn commitment ([extension](2017-01-01-eximbank-cn-zmb-005-china-eximbank-provides-3332-million-preferential)).

Neither fibre-length figure states whether it counts backbone only or backbone plus metropolitan and access network, which is why they cannot be reconciled ([length](2026-05-15-zambia-approves-k255m-digital-infrastructure), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094))).

A second communication towers programme reached 87.8 per cent disbursement on ministry reporting through a third-party database ([towers](2017-01-01-eximbank-cn-zmb-004-china-eximbank-provides-302-government-concessional)). One programme nearly drawn and one not drawn at all, both Chinese-financed, is the backbone record.

summary: A [cross-border fibre interconnector](2026-02-23 Zambia and Mozambique launch fibre-optic interconnector at Chanida–Cassacatiza border) was commissioned in February 2026 with no capacity, cost or funder stated, and a [terrestrial cable segment](2025-09-22 Google plans to build four subsea cable connectivity hubs for Africa) is stated ready for service in 2027.
developments:
The interconnector was commissioned in February 2026 ([interconnector](2026-02-23 Zambia and Mozambique launch fibre-optic interconnector at Chanida–Cassacatiza border), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094))).

The cable segment's 2027 date was first stated inside the window; the position itself did not move ([segment](2025-09-22 Google plans to build four subsea cable connectivity hubs for Africa), [investment](2024-05-28 Google invests in terrestrial-subsea cable linking Kenya to Australia)).

For a landlocked country these two routes are the whole of the international capacity record, and neither carries a capacity figure.

summary: [Internet adoption has been flat across two annual readings](2025-11-08-digital-2026-zambia-datareportal), and [mobile connections](2025-11-08-digital-2026-zambia-datareportal) count connections rather than people.
developments:
The adoption reading is cited rather than absorbed, and has been flat across two annual compilations ([users](2025-11-08-digital-2026-zambia-datareportal), [prior](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 - Zambia (DataReportal))).

Mobile connections are connections, not people, and the regulator's separate administrative series counts subscriptions per hundred inhabitants ([connections](2025-11-08-digital-2026-zambia-datareportal)).

A median fixed broadband download reading is likewise cited and not absorbed ([speed](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 - Zambia (DataReportal))). Every usage figure in this unit comes from a foreign compiler rather than the national regulator.

summary: The country is [among the top three African satellite markets](2026-07-22-starlink-26-african-markets-report) by June 2026 after entry in October 2023, and no national subscriber count, licence fee, contract term or procurement route is held.
developments:
Market entry was October 2023 and the country ranks among the top three African markets by June 2026 ([market](2026-07-22-starlink-26-african-markets-report), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094)), [chiefdom](2025-09-29-smart-zambia-starlink-moomba-chiefdom), [skills](2026-08-05-smart-zambia-itu-mpika-digital-skills)).

A top-three continental position with no licence fee, contract term or procurement route on record is worth stating as exactly that.

Direct-to-cell satellite trials name the country as a trial site on an operator statement, with no licence, spectrum decision or trial result held ([trials](2026-07-28-mtn-asante-leo-satellites-device-affordability-licence-passporting)).

summary: The [government wide area network](2026-08-05-zambia-border-connectivity-gwan-upgrade) declared phase one complete in March 2026 and had border-post gaps confirmed in August, and connected has at times meant completed site works rather than live service.
developments:
A primary of February 2025 establishes that connected has at times meant completed site works rather than live end-to-end service, which is the qualification every connection count in this unit needs ([network](2026-08-05-zambia-border-connectivity-gwan-upgrade), [deployment](2025-02-12-itweb-zambia-deploys-govt-wan-service-delivery), [councils](2026-03-25-kalemba-zambia-cdf-ecouncil-116-councils-gwan), [expansion](2026-07-08-smart-zambia-expands-digital-infrastructure)).

A border-post connectivity upgrade across five trade corridors set a national standard and commissioned an independent audit; the audit precedes the procurement rather than following it ([border](2026-08-05-zambia-border-connectivity-gwan-upgrade)).

Commissioning the audit before the procurement is the right order and is unusual in this frame.

2026-08-31 — a [further Northern Province district administration was connected and its staff oriented on the national portal and office collaboration tools, after which an official printed a road-tax document in his own office rather than travelling to the provincial centre](2026-08-31-techafricanews-zamportal-lupososhi-road-tax). It is the clearest published instance of a connection reaching a transaction, and it is one office: no district count, schedule or cost for the programme is published.

summary: A [memorandum on a national artificial-intelligence data centre](2026-06-08-zambia-huawei-ai-sovereignty-partnership) was signed with the vendor that built the existing [national data centre](2015-01-01-eximbank-cn-zmb-001-china-eximbank-provides-654-million-loan), and it precedes the strategy that would govern it.
developments:
The memorandum is not a contract; the same vendor built the existing national facility, and it precedes the National AI Strategy that would govern it ([memorandum](2026-06-08-zambia-huawei-ai-sovereignty-partnership)).

The existing facility's phase one commenced in January 2016 under a Chinese concessional loan, and it is the only domestic data-centre facility the base describes in physical terms ([centre](2015-01-01-eximbank-cn-zmb-001-china-eximbank-provides-654-million-loan)).

An edge data centre plan names the country among target countries on a company statement of intent rather than a commitment ([edge](2024-12-13 Nxtra - Airtel's leap into Africa's growing data center market)).

The commercial market can now be sized, and it is very small: [about five live facilities carrying roughly 2MW of live critical IT load at about 60 per cent occupancy, on roughly $5 million of annual revenue, with nothing under construction and a further 2MW or so in long-term pipeline](2025-07-01-data-centre-market-brief-zambia). Critical IT load per million people lags Botswana, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire and Ethiopia, and the estimate is an analyst's rather than an operator or regulator disclosure.

summary: [Load-shedding](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094)) is recorded as a constraint on digital services from the drought that began in January 2024, and [solar power at all 116 council offices](2026-03-25-kalemba-zambia-cdf-ecouncil-116-councils-gwan) is a government self-report.
developments:
The load-shedding statement comes from a lender appraisal; an eased-hours figure circulating elsewhere has no source in this base and is not carried ([load-shedding](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094))).

Solar power was stated complete for all 116 councils at a state institute briefing, with no capacity, cost, supplier or verification held ([solar](2026-03-25-kalemba-zambia-cdf-ecouncil-116-councils-gwan)).

Powering every council office while the grid constrains digital services generally is a sensible sequence, and the completion claim is the government's own.

About 650 priority health facilities carry solar power financed by an international health fund and a further 1,050 carry solar back-up power, on a base whose national electrification rate was about 44.5 per cent in 2023 and whose installed generation capacity is about 83 per cent hydroelectric ([case study](2025-04-01-zambia-digital-health-case-study)).

The same account puts internet connectivity in 883 health facilities ([case study](2025-04-01-zambia-digital-health-case-study)). A hydro-dominated grid in a country that has been load-shedding is the reason the backup is being financed facility by facility, and the financing partner rather than the utility is the one reporting it.

summary: The [cyber security agency](2026-08-22-zambiamonitor-zcsa-hate-speech-cyberbullying-warning) moved to new premises and issued a post-election warning, and [43,500 subscriber cards were deactivated](2026-08-04-zicta-blocks-43500-sim-cards-linked-to-scammers-secures-k19-8m) for mobile-money fraud in six months.
developments:
The agency's director general accounts for the move by saying it had been housed in the state institute's offices where space limited staff accommodation and key functions, and that the new premises let the whole team work together with access to its tools — which dates the constraint rather than measuring what it cost. No incident-response capability, staffing figure or service level is published before or after ([warning](2026-08-22-zambiamonitor-zcsa-hate-speech-cyberbullying-warning), [offices](2026-08-20-lusakatimes-zcsa-new-offices-cyber-incident-response), [trafficking](2026-07-30-zambia-ai-driven-human-trafficking-cyber-agency)).

The card deactivations cover January to June 2026 and are held as a paywalled lede ([deactivations](2026-08-04-zicta-blocks-43500-sim-cards-linked-to-scammers-secures-k19-8m)).

A company survey reports consumers targeted by digital fraud, with the comparison base shifted from one quarter's fieldwork window to another's ([fraud](2026-07-30-zambia-transunion-consumer-pulse-q1-2026-digital-fraud)).

summary: A [closed-circuit television bill and a national security command centre](2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition) are on the record in civil-society monitoring, and the [cyber agency artificial-intelligence remit](2026-07-30-zambia-ai-driven-human-trafficking-cyber-agency) is the first defined state mandate on file and is defensive.
developments:
The bill and command centre are recorded in monitoring current to late December 2025 ([bill](2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition)).

Artificial-intelligence-enabled trafficking and online scams were placed inside the cyber agency's response; it is the first defined state artificial-intelligence mandate on file, it is defensive, and it sits with the cyber regulator because no artificial-intelligence institution exists ([remit](2026-07-30-zambia-ai-driven-human-trafficking-cyber-agency), [surveillance](2025-04-18-us-warns-citizens-surveillance-law)).

The capital is listed among Chinese-supplied surveillance deployments in an eleven-country mapping; a widely quoted billion-dollar figure is a 2023 total across five countries, not a national figure and not current ([safe city](2026-03-01 Smart City Surveillance in Africa (IDS 2026)), [mapping](2023-09-27-ids-mapping-supply-surveillance-technologies-africa-1bn)).

summary: The [government service bus](2026-07-23-zambia-k22-million-collected-8-councils-electronic-payments-gsb) onboarded eight local authorities from June 2026, and a [named data-exchange layer](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD) is not the component through which the evidenced exchange work runs.
developments:
Eight local authorities were onboarded from June 2026, and no held source states how a separately named government bus relates to the service bus or to the national portal ([bus](2026-07-23-zambia-k22-million-collected-8-councils-electronic-payments-gsb), [statement](2023-06-16-zambia-zilas-ministerial-statement-parliament), [finances](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances)).

A data-exchange layer is named in the acceleration project appraisal as a complementary platform for data integration and exchange; the exchange work that is actually evidenced runs through the service bus, not through a component of that name ([layer](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094))).

Distinguishing the named component from the working one is what stops a project document being read as delivery.

The bus has a published service count behind it: [290 services were deployed on it by July 2024](2024-07-09-zambia-government-service-bus-services-update), alongside a citizens support portal, a public service portal and an electronic know-your-customer system. [Driving licence, road tax and vehicle registration applications run through the citizen-facing portal it sits under](2024-09-10-szi-rtsa-government-service-bus), where the queues that remain are for collecting licences that have not been printed. No exchange volume across the bus is published.

progress: Mixed, biometric enrolment progressing against a 2030 target while card issuance was deferred past the election
summary: [Biometric enrolment](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS) runs against a funded baseline of 1,500,000 people with digitally verifiable identity at December 2022 and a 4,000,000 target at October 2030, and [card issuance was deferred](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS) until after the August 2026 election.
developments:
The enrolment figure was given by the ministry to the state broadcaster ([enrolment](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS), [safeguards](2024-09-17 DPI Safeguards come online in Zambias next phase of digital integration), [switch](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch)).

Biometric card issuance was deferred to after the general election ([deferral](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS)).

A nationwide mobile campaign for 3.5m identity documents launched for a three-month run in April 2025, and its result is the largest single unreported outcome in the pre-window base ([campaign](2025-04-11 Zambia commences nationwide mobile campaign for issuance of 3.5M ID documents)). The paper card has been in issue since before independence, on the appraisal document's own wording rather than a published commencement date ([paper card](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD)).

summary: The [integrated registration information system](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch) reports end-to-end automation of birth and death notification under way, and the three enrolment figures held do not reconcile — a later source carrying a lower figure than an earlier one with no revision reported.
developments:
A later source carrying a lower figure than an earlier one, with no revision reported by any party, is the reconciliation problem stated plainly ([system](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch), [safeguards](2024-09-17 DPI Safeguards come online in Zambias next phase of digital integration), [enrolment](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS)).

Procurement of an international system integrator for an open-standards identity build opened in March 2026; the card is to carry registration-card functions plus travel and private-sector service access, and delivery dates diverge between the state ICT institute and the Registrar General ([procurement](2026-03-24 Zambia looking for MOSIP system integrator to support digital ID project), [training](2025-01-17 Zambia Advances Digital ID System with MOSIP Training for Healthcare Integration), [advance](2026-03-22-znbc-zambia-moves-ahead-digital-id-system)).

Two agencies giving different delivery dates for one credential is worth recording as the coordination question it is.

summary: [Transfer of the refugee registration database to the home affairs ministry](2024-09-05-worldbank-zambia-zrhcp-pad-padhi00410) is provided for as a project subcomponent, and two project documents give different card counts and values.
developments:
The safeguards framework gives US$6.5m and about 100,000 cards against the appraisal document's US$6m and about 150,000 ([transfer](2024-09-05-worldbank-zambia-zrhcp-pad-padhi00410)); the divergence is recorded, not resolved ([transfer](2024-09-05-worldbank-zambia-zrhcp-pad-padhi00410), [framework](2024-12-01-worldbank-zambia-zrhcp-environmental-social-management-framework), [engagement](2024-07-01-worldbank-zambia-zrhcp-stakeholder-engagement-plan)).

The parent project became effective in December 2024, and no disbursement figure, enrolment count or implementation progress within the window is held ([project](2024-09-27-world-bank-zambia-refugee-host-communities-grant), [plans](2025-10-03 Zambia plans domestic digital ID development with help from international partners)).

Moving a refugee database from an international agency to a ministry is a change of controller, and the country's data-protection regulator has no recorded action of any kind.

summary: The [birth registration rate](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS) is an external agency figure cited by the Registrar General, so a 50 per cent target for end-2026 has no measured mid-point on file.
developments:
The rate is cited rather than measured domestically ([rate](2025-12-28 Over 1.3 Million Citizens Enrolled on INRIS), [target](2025-06-12 Zambia says using multiple strategies to meet 50 percent birth registration goal by 2026)).

Civil registration runs on a three-pillar strategy stated at a continental civil registration day ([registration](2025-08-12 Zambia sees civil registration as bedrock of inclusive digital transformation)), and a modernisation programme was launched on the same three pillars ([programme](2025-08-12 Zambia sees civil registration as bedrock of inclusive digital transformation)).

A target with no measured mid-point, four months from its date, is the position.

summary: The [integrated land administration system](2023-06-16-zambia-zilas-ministerial-statement-parliament) went live in May 2023, and the minister told Parliament the predecessor ran with no maintenance contract from March 2022, creating a conduit for corruption.
developments:
The system went live after data migration from the predecessor ([system](2023-06-16-zambia-zilas-ministerial-statement-parliament), [clearance](2023-09-19-zambia-zilas-digital-clearance-corpus-legal), [gateway](2024-09-13 ZILAS - Your Gateway to Modern Land Administration (SMART Zambia)), [expansion](2026-07-08-smart-zambia-expands-digital-infrastructure)).

The minister's statement that the predecessor ran unmaintained for over a year, creating a conduit for corruption, is a government account of its own prior failure and is the most specific such statement in this ledger.

The denominator is now on record and it is the finding: [fewer than 450,000 of an estimated 1.2 million numbered properties hold registered title deeds, and about 45,000 owners pay ground rent, yielding roughly K157 million a year against more than K1.2 billion if compliance improved](2026-01-08-fixing-land-records-central-zambia-development-agenda). That 1.2 million excludes customary land entirely, so the untitled share of the country is larger than the ratio suggests.

summary: A [national spatial data infrastructure policy and portal](2026-07-08-smart-zambia-expands-digital-infrastructure) was launched, and a [national carbon registry](2026-08-08-govt-launches-national-carbon-registry) launched with counts given by the permanent secretary.
developments:
The spatial policy and portal were launched in the capital; the event date is inferred from a relative reference in a June 2026 report, and the policy document itself is not held ([spatial](2026-07-08-smart-zambia-expands-digital-infrastructure), [open source](2026-06-17 Zambia's govt leans towards open-source)).

The carbon registry's launch counts — more than 90 carbon projects at stages of approval, and bilateral agreements with three European states — are the permanent secretary's own ([registry](2026-08-08-govt-launches-national-carbon-registry)), and no public access, transaction count, custodian ministry or disclosure rule for its holdings is stated ([holdings](2026-08-07-zambia-national-carbon-registry-launch)).

A registry of tradeable environmental assets with no published disclosure rule is worth naming as the transparency question it is.

summary: The [national financial switch](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch) has its cost-reduction objective stated on record as not yet delivered, and [cheque acceptance is to stop](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch) on a date sourced from a single sentence about another country.
developments:
The electronic clearing house is stated as not yet live on the regional instant-payment scheme, and central bank interest in the continental system is characterised as conversation rather than commitment ([switch](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch)).

The cheque stop date comes from a single sentence in an article about another country, and no central bank circular is held ([cheques](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch), [comparator](2026-01-13 The rise of cheques as Kenya's preferred payment method)).

Ending an instrument on a date evidenced only in foreign coverage is a limit on what this report can state about the transition.

summary: The [government payment gateway](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances) puts cumulative collections at over K8.8 billion with no stated start date, and the two [digital revenue figures](2026-07-23-zambia-k22-million-collected-8-councils-electronic-payments-gsb) cover different periods and issuers.
developments:
The collection total has no stated start date, so it is a cumulative figure of unknown period ([gateway](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094)), [property](2026-05-13-zambia-launches-pmis-property-management)).

The two revenue figures cover different periods and issuers and are not a like-for-like series ([revenue](2026-07-23-zambia-k22-million-collected-8-councils-electronic-payments-gsb), [investment](2026-03-25-zanis-smart-zambia-digital-infrastructure-investment), [finances](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances)).

A cumulative total of unknown period and two non-comparable figures are what the revenue record supports.

summary: The [social cash transfer](2026-08-22-zambiamonitor-social-cash-transfer-july-august-2026) began its July-August 2026 cycle disbursement, on the ministry's own figures with no redemption rate, provider list or exclusion figure published.
developments:
The cycle disbursement began in August 2026 ([disbursement](2026-08-22-zambiamonitor-social-cash-transfer-july-august-2026)).

A provincial minister separately names four districts where poor network service blocks access to social cash transfers and farm input subsidies, so the exclusion figure nobody publishes is the one that would measure whether the transfer arrives.

summary: [Financial inclusion among adults](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch) rose on a national consumer survey published by the central bank, with the survey month not stated, and [securities exchange app users](2026-08-17-digital-push-powers-zambian-bourse) rose on the exchange's own registration figure.
developments:
The inclusion figure is carried at year precision because the survey month is not stated ([inclusion](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch)).

The exchange figure is for registered users, not active traders or funded accounts ([app users](2026-08-17-digital-push-powers-zambian-bourse)).

Registered rather than active, and a survey with no stated month, are the two qualifications every uptake claim in this unit carries.

summary: A [regional retail payments platform](2026-08-10-comesa-clearing-house-drpp-scheme-rulebook-gender-strategy) published its scheme rulebook and a gender strategy, and [currency onboarding to the regional settlement system](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking) is attributed to the system's operator rather than the national central bank.
developments:
The corridor with a neighbour is the one the platform runs on; no national transaction volume, participant count or fee schedule is published ([platform](2026-08-10-comesa-clearing-house-drpp-scheme-rulebook-gender-strategy)).

The currency onboarding is a statement of intent attributed to the system's operator, not to the national central bank ([onboarding](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking), [switch](2026-07-27-zambia-from-rails-to-routine-national-financial-switch)).

Card acceptance was extended to nine African markets with merchant and card counts given as the two companies' own and no country-specific figure ([cards](2026-08-19-tan-unionpay-standard-bank-nine-african-markets)).

summary: A [national electronic health record](2026-07-16-zambia-govlink-private-4g-techafricanews) is deployed at about 80 per cent of health facilities, and the identity-integration account is implementer-authored and promotional with no independent evaluation held.
developments:
The deployment share was reported in July 2026 ([record](2026-07-16-zambia-govlink-private-4g-techafricanews), [presentation](2025-03-01-smartcare-pro-programme-managers-presentation), [expansion](2026-07-08-smart-zambia-expands-digital-infrastructure), [rural](2026-01-15 How Digital Public Infrastructure Is Transforming Health and Identity in Rural Zambia)).

A hospital edition pilot launched at a teaching hospital, and whether it shares the national record's fingerprint enrolment or the open-standards identifier is not established ([pilot](2026-04-28-zambia-smartcare-2-0-ndola-pilot)).

An emergency outbreak response platform is in two-day user-acceptance testing rather than in service, with no go-live date, hosting arrangement or data-governance rule published ([outbreak](2026-08-19-cidrz-zebra-outbreak-response-platform-zambia)). Eighty per cent facility coverage is among the highest in this frame, and the evaluation behind it is the implementer's.

summary: [Satellite terminals were installed in rural public facilities](2025-09-29-smart-zambia-starlink-moomba-chiefdom) and a [government private fourth-generation network](2026-07-16-zambia-govlink-private-4g-itweb) launched at a teaching hospital.
developments:
The state buying foreign satellite capacity for the last mile sits alongside a government-owned private network build ([terminals](2025-09-29-smart-zambia-starlink-moomba-chiefdom), [network](2026-07-16-zambia-govlink-private-4g-techafricanews)).

The private network launched at a teaching hospital; clinician accounts at the launch site are operator statements, and no baseline or measured outcome is held ([launch](2026-07-16-zambia-govlink-private-4g-itweb), [coverage](2026-07-16-zambia-govlink-private-4g-techafricanews)).

Two connectivity strategies for the same problem — buying foreign satellite capacity and building a state network — running at once, with no source relating them.

summary: A [contract tracking and management system](2026-07-12-govt-launches-ctmis-contract-system) was launched with the justice ministry, held as a paywalled lede with no volume or turnaround figure published.
developments:
It was launched in July 2026 ([system](2026-07-12-govt-launches-ctmis-contract-system)).

It is the only justice-sector system in this ledger, and what it does is known only from a headline.

summary: A [memorandum on border post scanning and security technology](2026-08-25-diggers-zra-astrophysics-border-security-technology) was signed in August 2026, with no commitment amount, equipment specification or delivery timetable stated.
developments:
It was signed on 24 August 2026 ([memorandum](2026-08-25-diggers-zra-astrophysics-border-security-technology)).

It sits alongside the border-post connectivity upgrade recorded separately, and no source relates the two — scanning equipment and the network it would report over, procured on different tracks.

summary: The [national portal](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances) reports over 400 services onboarded — a figure stated for the service bus, gateway, portal and payment platform together rather than the portal alone — and an [electronic government amendment bill](2026-01-23 Zambia begins amending Electronic Government Act) is in development.
developments:
The 400-plus figure covers four systems together, not the portal alone ([portal](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094)), [councils](2026-05-29-councils-digital-lcc-first-zamportal)).

Government services online were counted at a trade fair against a denominator that is the appraisal's estimate and is not restated in the newer figure ([services](2026-07-10-digital-services-strengthen-zambia-finances)).

The amendment bill was presented at a stakeholder meeting, with officials naming fragmented, vendor-locked systems as a governance and legal problem rather than a technical one ([bill](2026-01-23 Zambia begins amending Electronic Government Act), [corruption](2026-01-24-digitisation-reduced-corruption-smart-zambia)). An online passport system launched with over 1,000 passports processed at launch ([passports](2026-01-08 Zambia unveils online passport application system)).

Authentication has been separated out into a service of its own: [ZamPass runs as the national authentication and access control service from the government service bus domain, with companion mobile applications and a consent endpoint](2026-01-01-zampass). It is a single-page application that publishes nothing about its enrolment base, the identities it authenticates against, or which services sit behind it.

summary: A [smart office management system](2025-06-23-smart-office-system-rollout) demonstrated in June 2025 has not moved — the clearest pre-window baseline in this ledger that has not — and a [property management system](2026-05-13-zambia-launches-pmis-property-management) launched in May 2026.
developments:
The office system was demonstrated at health ministry headquarters with one province selected as pilot, and has not moved since ([office](2025-06-23-smart-office-system-rollout)).

The property management system was launched by the infrastructure ministry with the state ICT institute ([property](2026-05-13-zambia-launches-pmis-property-management)).

A digital loan system for civil servants was briefed to the microfinance association at a courtesy call, with no agreement or memorandum reported ([loans](2026-08-07-smart-zambia-and-amiz-explore-digital-loan-system-for-civil-servants)).

progress: Mixed, three different council counts measuring three different things
summary: [Eight of 116 councils](2026-08-03-lcc-urges-businesses-to-embrace-e-council-platform) are on the electronic council platform, [one is live on the national portal](2026-05-29-councils-digital-lcc-first-zamportal), and all 116 are network-connected — three counts measuring three different things.
developments:
Eight local authorities were onboarded to the council platform from June 2026; a March account names seven of a stated eight, and the platform's own launch date is not established ([platform](2026-08-03-lcc-urges-businesses-to-embrace-e-council-platform), [councils](2026-03-25-kalemba-zambia-cdf-ecouncil-116-councils-gwan), [collections](2026-07-23-zambia-k22-million-collected-8-councils-electronic-payments-gsb)).

One council went live as the first of 116 on the national portal; that is distinct from network connection of all 116 and from platform onboarding, and the three counts measure different things ([portal](2026-05-29-councils-digital-lcc-first-zamportal)).

A constituency fund management system has data entry under way with full operationalisation stated for June 2026 ([fund](2026-03-25-kalemba-zambia-cdf-ecouncil-116-councils-gwan)), and one town council was equipped with connectivity and telepresence in August 2026 with no programme size, cost or council list published ([equipment](2026-08-26-sinazongwe-smart-zambia-ict-deployment-techafricanews)).

summary: An implementing partner published a first-hand account of [artificial-intelligence automation at the National Assembly](2026-07-28-idinsight-responsible-ai-african-parliaments), and the same finding is reported from two other African parliaments.
developments:
That the same finding appears in three parliaments makes it a pattern rather than an incident ([parliament](2026-07-28-idinsight-responsible-ai-african-parliaments)).

An artificial-intelligence for public good challenge closed applications in August 2026; it is a call for applications, with no award value, cohort size or deployment commitment by any of the five institutions stated ([challenge](2026-08-18-undp-zambia-ai-for-public-good-challenge)).

summary: A [feature-phone artificial-intelligence voice service](2026-01-15 Leveraging AI to Bypass the Smartphone Barrier and Advance Digital Inclusion in Africa) is the only such application on file reaching people directly, and an [international laboratory](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge) is on offer with no agreement signed.
developments:
The voice service is cited as a deployed feature-phone application and is the only artificial-intelligence application on file reaching people directly ([service](2026-01-15 Leveraging AI to Bypass the Smartphone Barrier and Advance Digital Inclusion in Africa)).

The laboratory was disclosed as an opportunity with no agreement signed; it is the only national-level artificial-intelligence institution on offer, and no domestic body exists ([laboratory](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge)).

A country whose only direct-to-citizen artificial-intelligence service runs over feature phones, and whose only institutional option is an offer, is where the record stands.

summary: An [innovation hub](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge) ran the nine-month pipeline that took a national team to global finals, and its chief executive says the talent pool is real but investment in research, technology and innovation is not.
developments:
The chief executive's statement is his own account, given at the same event ([hub](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge)).

A digital economy incubator recruited facilitators and group coaches in August 2026; it is European Union-funded and delivered by a private hub with a non-governmental organisation, with no cohort size, budget or start date stated ([incubator](2026-08-06-european-union-zambia-bongohive-ignite-facilitators)).

One agricultural technology company exists because European traceability-compliance software was quoted at thousands to tens of thousands of dollars a month, on the founders' own account, with no revenue, farmer count, funding or independent evaluation held ([company](2026-07-31-green-giraffe-ai-farmers-zambia)).

summary: A [Startup Bill](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge) was named by a ministry representative — its first and only mention in the base — and a [technology company listed](2026-05-14-zambia-accelerate-digital-economy-ppp) on the domestic securities exchange.
developments:
The bill's mention is the first and only one in the base ([bill](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge)).

The listing is described as recent ([listing](2026-05-14-zambia-accelerate-digital-economy-ppp)), and a company founded in 2025 was profiled in July 2026 ([company](2026-07-21-dalitso-mbewe-padue-zambie)).

A continental diversity report's third edition gives the female co-founder and chief executive share; the underlying report is not held and only the trade-press account is ([diversity](2026-08-04-diversity-dividend-female-startup-cofounders)).

summary: The [regulator annual market performance report](2023-03-13-zicta-2022-annual-market-report-subscriptions) for 2022 is the latest market sizing held, with the article's own dollar conversions undated as to rate.
developments:
It is the regulator's 2022 annual report, reaching the base through a news account whose dollar conversions carry no stated rate date ([report](2023-03-13-zicta-2022-annual-market-report-subscriptions)).

Four years without a newer regulator market report, in a unit whose usage figures otherwise come from foreign compilers, is the measurement gap at the base of this whole ledger.

summary: [ICT equipment was handed to a youth resource centre](2026-08-05-smart-zambia-itu-mpika-digital-skills) under a transformation centres initiative, with no cost, contract term, procurement route or trainee count published.
developments:
The handover was made in August 2026 ([centres](2026-08-05-smart-zambia-itu-mpika-digital-skills), [challenge](2026-07-17-zambia-ai-leadership-robotics-challenge)).

A digital literacy programme in six schools recorded core funding disbursed for the 2025 activity year; it is a commitment record rather than a delivery report, with no pupil count, equipment or outcome stated ([schools](2025-01-01-iati-xm-dac-21-1-2025000879b2miscara-digital-literacy-six-zambian-schools)).

Two literacy items, neither with a published outcome, is the whole of general digital literacy here.

summary: [146 officers were trained](2026-07-20-smart-zambia-trains-146-district-officers-southern-province) in digital skills and data protection across three district administrations — a single-province tranche rather than a coverage measure.
developments:
The training covered three district administrations in one province ([training](2026-07-20-smart-zambia-trains-146-district-officers-southern-province)).

Naming it a tranche rather than a coverage measure is the point: no national civil-service digital training figure exists in this base, and 146 officers in one province cannot stand for one.

summary: A [digital skills and capabilities component](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD) was board-approved within the acceleration grant, and a [vendor academy training commitment](2026-06-08-zambia-huawei-ai-sovereignty-partnership) was included in the artificial-intelligence data centre memorandum.
developments:
The skills component was board-approved with its parent grant in September 2025 ([component](2025-09-11 DZAP World Bank PAD), [appraisal](2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094))).

The vendor training reports no start date, cost, curriculum or intake process ([academy](2026-06-08-zambia-huawei-ai-sovereignty-partnership)).

Both are components of larger instruments rather than programmes with their own delivery record, which is why neither carries an intake figure.

2026-08-31 — a ride-hailing company's STEM fellowship, [begun in Zambia in 2024 with 30 students, expanded into a pan-African programme across six countries and selected 24 fellows from more than 600 applications](2026-08-31-techafricanews-yango-fellowship-six-countries), with a graduation and pitch day set for Abidjan on 17-19 September 2026. The 2026 cohort is smaller than the single-country intake it grew from, and no per-country allocation, financial value or outcome is published — an expansion in reach rather than in scale.

summary: The revenue authority signed a [research memorandum and a non-disclosure agreement](2026-07-17-zambia-revenue-authority-ictd-deal), so the terms — and whether taxpayer microdata moves — are not disclosed.
developments:
The memorandum and the accompanying non-disclosure agreement were signed in July 2026 ([memorandum](2026-07-17-zambia-revenue-authority-ictd-deal)).

A research agreement whose confidentiality clause conceals whether taxpayer microdata moves is worth recording as exactly that, in a country whose data-protection regulator has no recorded action.

The domestic base has a date and a founding source: [the university's computing and informatics department was established in September 1998 with Belgian development funding through a university cooperation programme](2025-01-01-zambia-department-of-computing-and-informatics), which paid for the refurbishment, the equipment and two networked laboratories across two five-year phases meant to end in self-sufficiency. [It opened with a postgraduate diploma and admitted its first degree students in August 2000](2025-01-01-zambia-department-of-computing-and-informatics).

summary: The [Universal Access and Service Fund](2026-06-17-zicta-assesses-uasf-projects-muchinga) has no fund size, levy rate, annual disbursement or cumulative tower count held for any year, under [2012 regulations](2012-06-15-zambia-si-38-2012-ict-universal-access-regulations) that are its regulatory basis.
developments:
A board assessment tour of projects in three provinces took place in 2026, and no fund size, levy rate, annual disbursement or cumulative tower count is held for any year ([fund](2026-06-17-zicta-assesses-uasf-projects-muchinga), [projects](2025-09-01-zicta-uasf-copperbelt-northwestern), [bill](2026-07-23-zambia-postal-courier-services-bill-2026)).

The regulations were gazetted in June 2012 and are the fund's regulatory basis; the fund's own size, current levy collected and annual disbursement remain not held ([regulations](2012-06-15-zambia-si-38-2012-ict-universal-access-regulations)).

Fourteen years of a universal access fund with no published financial figure of any kind is the single largest accountability gap in this ledger.

summary: A [satellite and artificial-intelligence farm traceability platform](2026-07-31-green-giraffe-ai-farmers-zambia) is in use on the founder's account, with no user count, revenue or independent verification.
developments:
The platform is described in a founder interview ([platform](2026-07-31-green-giraffe-ai-farmers-zambia)).

It is the only earth-observation application in this ledger, and it exists because compliance software priced for European buyers was out of reach — which makes a traceability requirement in one market the origin of a domestic technology company in another.

summary: A [United States health financing memorandum](2026-07-30-world-insights-us-health-aid-meets-resistance-across-africa) was reported shelved over data terms and a minerals precondition, and the health minister denied the mining link and was dismissed three days later without explanation.
developments:
The memorandum was reported shelved in May 2026 ([shelving](2026-07-30-world-insights-us-health-aid-meets-resistance-across-africa), [exploitation](2026-02-25 US accused of 'shameless exploitation' over proposed Zambian health aid deal), [rejection](2026-02-26 Zambia rejects U.S. health aid over mining partnership ties)).

The minister denied the mining link on 15 February 2026 and was dismissed three days later without explanation. The 25-year data term is reported from a leaked draft rather than a text this base holds, and the value is given as US$1.012bn in that draft and as up to US$2bn by the foreign minister in May 2026, with the two unreconciled ([stress test](2026-03-27 Kenya's Health Deal Is a Stress Test for the America First Global Health Strategy), [investigation](2026-07-23-propublica-us-health-data-agreements-africa-digital-colonialism)).

A country declining a health financing agreement over its data terms is rare in this frame and is recorded as the position it is.

summary: A [bilateral seminar set out sovereignty conditions](2026-08-17-zambia-ai-sovereignty-conditions-china-cooperation) for digital cooperation with no agreement signed, against Chinese financing of the national data centre, the backbone and the towers programme.
developments:
Sovereignty conditions were set out at the seminar and no agreement was signed; the source body is an excerpt rather than a full capture ([seminar](2026-08-17-zambia-ai-sovereignty-conditions-china-cooperation), [ties](2026-06-08 Zambia, China deepen digital ties), [support](2026-08-07-techbytes-china-reaffirms-support-for-zambias-digital-transformation)).

The existing relationship is not a matter of intention: Chinese concessional finance built the national data centre, funded the towers programme to the disbursement level recorded elsewhere in this report and left the backbone extension wholly undrawn, and the same vendor holds the artificial-intelligence data centre memorandum.

Setting conditions on future cooperation while the installed base is already Chinese-financed is the position the record supports.

summary: The technology ministry puts the country at [about 26.2 million mobile subscriptions in 2025 against 23.2 million in 2024](2026-08-28-lusakatimes-zambia-cyber-security-capacity).
developments: The technology ministry put the country at about 26.2 million mobile subscriptions in 2025, up from 23.2 million in 2024, with about 14.7 million of them mobile internet ([ministry](2026-08-28-lusakatimes-zambia-cyber-security-capacity)). These are the ministry's own figures, given in a seminar address rather than a regulator publication.

summary: [Data interoperability standards are mandatory for every ministry, province and spending agency](2024-01-01-szi-data-interoperability-standards), with an annual compliance audit schedule.
developments:
The state ICT institute issued public service ICT data interoperability standards that bind every ministry, province and spending agency, and carry an annual compliance audit schedule ([standards](2024-01-01-szi-data-interoperability-standards)).

Together with the electronic government statute they set the data management and governance requirements for government data ([scope](2024-01-01-szi-data-interoperability-standards)).

No audit finding, compliance rate or exemption is published, so whether the standards are met is not established - and officials pursuing the statute's amendment still name fragmented, vendor-locked systems as the problem.

summary: The [education management information system was built in one district](2025-01-01-zambia-education-management-system-emis-user-story), replacing annual school returns keyed into a desktop database.
developments:
An implementing partner, working with the education ministry and a UN agency, built the system on the open-source platform already used for the national water and sanitation programme, from 2016 and in one district ([system](2025-01-01-zambia-education-management-system-emis-user-story)).

Before it, the ministry depended on annual reports from schools entered into a desktop database, which meant attendance and termly standardised exam scores were never captured at all ([before](2025-01-01-zambia-education-management-system-emis-user-story)).

Nothing on record states that the district implementation has been extended nationally, and no enrolment, attendance or school coverage figure from the system is published.

summary: [9,163 companies were registered between January and May 2026](2026-07-03-pacra-registers-9163-companies-jan-may-2026), a 7 per cent increase on the same months of 2025.
developments:
[The registration agency reported 9,163 companies incorporated between January and May 2026, against 8,551 in the same months of 2025](2026-07-03-pacra-registers-9163-companies-jan-may-2026), a rise of 7 per cent.

[Transport and storage recorded the highest sectoral growth at 17 per cent](2026-07-03-pacra-registers-9163-companies-jan-may-2026), on expansion in logistics, freight, courier and warehousing services, and the agency names formalisation of micro, small and medium enterprises as the reform it is pursuing.

What is published is a flow, not a stock: no register size, no count of active companies and no measure of the business base the register covers accompanies it.

summary: The [Lusaka exchange carries 12 peers on 76G of capacity](2024-08-02-zambia-lsk-ix-exchange-record), 10 of them open to new peering.
developments:
[The exchange's peering record lists 12 peers over 12 connections, 10 of them open, on 76G of total capacity with full support for the newer addressing protocol](2024-08-02-zambia-lsk-ix-exchange-record).

Traffic statistics are linked from the record rather than carried on it, and the record discloses no founding date ([record](2024-08-02-zambia-lsk-ix-exchange-record)).

No regulator statement of traffic exchanged locally, and no figure for what share of national traffic stays in-country rather than transiting abroad, is held.

summary: The [2022 census national analytical report was published in August 2025](2025-08-01-zambia-census-literacy-education), putting the literacy rate for those aged five and over at 62.6 per cent.
developments:
[The twelve-chapter national analytical report of the 2022 census was released in August 2025](2025-08-01-zambia-census-literacy-education).

[It puts the national literacy rate for those aged five and over at 62.6 per cent, 65.3 for males and 60.1 for females, and 78.2 per cent in urban areas against 49.8 in rural ones](2025-08-01-zambia-census-literacy-education); [the rate for those aged 15 to 24 is 77.1 per cent](2025-08-01-zambia-census-literacy-education), and [the figure for those aged five and over has risen from 55.3 per cent in 2000](2025-08-01-zambia-census-literacy-education).

No release calendar is held, so what else the agency has scheduled is not established.

summary: The social cash transfer [reached 1,555,840 households in February 2026](2026-02-20-social-cash-transfer-reaches-156-million-households), up from 1.3 million, after 305,000 were added against a plan for 250,000.
developments:
[The ministry reported the nationwide scale-up complete in February 2026, taking coverage from 1.3 million to 1,555,840 households](2026-02-20-social-cash-transfer-reaches-156-million-households).

[More than 300,000 households were added where 250,000 had been planned for 2025](2026-02-20-social-cash-transfer-reaches-156-million-households), which the minister attributed to the reach of the sensitisation campaign and to demand.

The count is the ministry's own, given at a press briefing, with no independent verification held, and it sits against a unified national social registry approved by cabinet in April 2025 that is still in early implementation.

summary: Networking equipment for [40 police stations was delivered in February 2026](2026-02-03-smart-zambia-police-digitalisation-40-stations) under a local-area-network and last-mile connectivity project.
developments:
[Routers, switches, access points and firewalls were delivered to the state ICT institute in February 2026 for deployment to 40 police stations nationwide](2026-02-03-smart-zambia-police-digitalisation-40-stations), under a police local area network and last mile connectivity project intended to connect stations to a centralised system and move records and processes online.

[The equipment was supplied by a domestic ICT firm](2026-02-03-smart-zambia-police-digitalisation-40-stations).

The equipment is delivered rather than installed: no station list, timetable, budget or go-live statement is published, and no count of stations already connected is held.
